_doc: SHARED VECTORS for the derived unit-admission rule: ADR-0008's model as
amended by ADR-0009 (a density unlocks the other family), ADR-0010 (piece
is an admission fact) and ADR-0014 (all to all — the kitchen trim is gone,
a family is admitted whole, and the household prunes per row).
Two implementations claim to apply the same rule: the Dart one the app
offers chips from (lib/features/ingredients/domain/allowed_units.dart,
`allowedUnitsFor`) and the SQL one the server materializes allowed_units
with (default_allowed_units()). Each shape below is a real row somebody
types — a jar of yeast, a bag of flour, one avocado — written once so
neither side can drift alone.
Who reads this file:
- app/test/features/ingredients/allowed_units_test.dart loops it directly.
- supabase/seed/scripts/gen_admission_vectors.ts renders it as the
generated `values` block in supabase/tests/unit_admission.sql, and the
test beside that script fails if the committed block has drifted.
`expect` is in the app's DISPLAY order, which is what allowedUnitsFor
returns. The SQL function emits its own order (basis family first,
whatever the default unit is), so the generated pgTAP block compares the
two lists as SETS. Membership is the mirror; order is each side's own
business.
`basis` is the macros basis — 'g' for per-100 g rows, 'ml' for per-100 ml.
`density` is g per ml, or null for a row that has none yet.

vectors.why: a spoon default with no density says the whole mass family and no volume unit at all — being sold by the spoon does not make spoons convertible
a cup default with a density: both families whole, twelve chips, and the household prunes what it will never say
a spoon default with a density: both families plus the oil class's imprecise words — nobody takes a handful of oil
a count default with no density: its own piece, the whole basis family, and the one imprecise word produce earns
the seasoning category admits the whole imprecise tail, and the spoons still need a density like everyone else's
a count default WITH a density admits the volume family whole — "1 cup diced mango" is a real line, and so is half a litre of purée
the same rule under the row ADR-0010's curation pass trims: the DERIVED list still offers piece, which is exactly what a curated list then takes away
a per-ml row's volume default IS its basis family, so it stands alone — the whole volume ladder, and no gram leg until a density arrives
the same per-ml row once it has a density: the mass family unlocks behind the basis family
a gram default on its own basis family says the whole mass family, and no volume without a density
the same family entered from the customary end: a pound default admits exactly what a gram default does
an ounce default with a density: the mass family plus the volume family the density bridges to, fl oz included — it is an ordinary kitchen unit here
